The clamour among Liverpool supporters for more incomings before the transfer window closed on Tuesday night was understandable.
An unconvincing start to the season had only served to intensify concerns over whether they possess sufficient quality and depth at right-back and in midfield.
Neither department has been strengthened, and it requires a sizeable leap of faith to believe those areas of weakness can simply be addressed by new head coach Andoni Iraola working with what he’s got on the training field.
Advertisement
Jeremie Frimpong has struggled in the opening two matches in the ongoing absence of injured first-choice right-back Conor Bradley. The debate over the balance of the midfield will rumble on with no specialist No 6 brought in and teenager Trey Nyoni backed to step up following the sale of Curtis Jones to Inter.
However, at the top end of the pitch, Liverpool’s inactivity in the market once they had finalised Bradley Barcola’s protracted £123million ($166.5m) move from Paris Saint-Germain should be welcomed.
Rewind to Sunday and it looked increasingly likely that Cody Gakpo was going to be sold to Manchester City for around £80m.
The former PSV forward had informed Liverpool that he was keen on the move. There had also been strong interest from Tottenham Hotspur but City was his preferred destination.
Sanctioning that deal was always dependent on Liverpool being able to recruit a suitable replacement for the Netherlands international at an acceptable price.
They had to consider whether to increase their offer for Yankuba Minteh having previously had bids of £50m and £60m rejected by Brighton & Hove Albion. There had also been contact with Crystal Palace over a potential deal for Ismaila Sarr.
Ultimately, common sense prevailed. Selling Gakpo and bringing in either Minteh or Sarr would have been a big mistake. Yes, Minteh and Sarr both operate on the right and buying one of them arguably would have provided a better balance to Iraola’s attacking department given that his other wide players prefer the left flank.
But in terms of talent, either would have been a downgrade on Gakpo. Minteh, 22, who is out for around two months after having surgery on his right leg, scored three goals and provided four assists in 34 Premier League matches last season.
Sarr, who always seems to shine against Liverpool, fared better with nine goals and an assist in 28 league matches for Palace in 2025-26, but paying more than £60m for the Senegal international, who turns 29 in February, wouldn’t have been a smart investment.
Advertisement
Captain Virgil van Dijk had left nobody in any doubt about his stance on the matter when he spoke to reporters after last Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest. “I want Cody to stay not only because he’s a quality player but also because he’s a friend of mine,” Van Dijk said. “He’s very important for us. I think we should keep quality players.”
On Monday afternoon, having considered their options, Liverpool pulled the plug as they rejected City’s offer and Gakpo was informed that he would be staying put. He accepted the decision and trained with Iraola’s squad as normal on Tuesday.
When a player asks to join a rival club and the move doesn’t subsequently materialise it can often leave him in an uncomfortable position regarding his relationship with the supporters. But it would be crazy if Gakpo faced any kind of backlash.
For a start, you can understand why he wanted to leave given Liverpool had just spent so much money on Barcola, who plays in his favoured role on the left wing, and the club were clearly prepared to offload him. You can also understand why he wanted to join Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City rather than Tottenham given his ambition to win more silverware.
The fickle nature of football won’t have been lost on Gakpo. Last season he faced a torrent of abuse on social media as he struggled for form. Recently those same platforms have been awash with praise and fans demanding that he remained at Liverpool.
Some were far too quick to forget how influential he was in the title-winning campaign of 2024-25 under Arne Slot when he scored 18 goals in all competitions. He was one of many in that dressing room to lose their way last term, but he’s looked refreshed and energised since Iraola took over this summer.
In fact he’s arguably been Liverpool’s best attacking player in the opening two Premier League matches — scoring in the 2-2 draw at Newcastle United with a clinical finish from outside the box and providing a pinpoint assist for Alexander Isak to fire home against Forest.
Advertisement
Iraola starting him in both games despite all the noise about his future says a lot about how he’s conducted himself on and off the pitch throughout this summer. He didn’t agitate for a move, he didn’t down tools. As Liverpool battled in vain to find a late winner against Forest, Gakpo was as animated as anyone on the touchline after Rio Ngumoha came off the bench to replace him.
From a business perspective, it’s easy to see why banking £80m for Gakpo carried some appeal for Liverpool given that he cost them £44m from PSV in January 2023.
But football-wise, it would have been wrong on a few levels. Firstly, it would have strengthened Manchester City. No player has moved directly between the clubs since Raheem Sterling went to the Etihad in 2015. Given how they have gone toe to toe for so much of the past decade and the subsequent levels of animosity, the sale would not have sat right.
More significantly, it would have weakened Liverpool. Imagine having an injured Minteh rather than Gakpo, and then Isak picking up a knock in the coming weeks.
Gakpo staying means that Liverpool have proper cover for Isak through the middle until Hugo Ekitike returns from his Achilles injury around the midway point of the campaign.
Barcola is expected to predominantly operate off the left but the France international might need some time to get up to speed given that he hasn’t played since the World Cup.
Gakpo’s versatility makes him a real asset with Iraola starting him on the right against Forest and Victor Munoz on the other flank. In the latter stages, it was Ngumoha on the left with Munoz on the right.
With Friday’s trip to newly-promoted Ipswich Town — the first of five games in the space of 16 days — there will be plenty of game time to go round.
Liverpool’s priority all summer was to buy pace out wide and they achieved it with the exciting signings of Munoz and Barcola. Jeremy Jacquet looks like a decent replacement for Ibrahima Konate and getting Ronald Araujo on loan provides extra cover given the defensive injuries.
Advertisement
The fear remains that they will pay the price in the months ahead for not doing more in the market given the issues at full-back and in midfield, but there’s certainly no shortage of firepower.
A few days ago it looked like Barcola was going to be followed through the door by another attacking acquisition. However, given that would have meant sending Gakpo to the Etihad, Liverpool were right to stick with what they had.

No amount of transfer outlay can make Enzo Maresca's Manchester City task straightforward. Following greats is hard, even for very talented coaches.
Some of the pre-season conversation saw the likes of Unai Emery and David Moyes mentioned alongside Maresca. They succeeded Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson at Arsenal and Manchester United respectively and never really had a chance. How on earth can Maresca hope to follow Pep Guardiola successfully?
Emery and Moyes will be mentioned again after any moments of turbulence at the Etihad Stadium this season. Their cautionary tales were cited after Arsenal swept past City 3-0 in the Community Shield. There was a gulf, an unbridgeable chasm.
Of course, part of that was overreaction after a glorified friendly. The narrative of Arsenal being a stable and assured force while half of the Premier League is in flux also appeals to purists' instincts. Other teams are spending hundreds of millions of pounds and sacking managers, just to try to catch up with a team that charted a steady course, trusted the process and finally won the league.
On the evidence of the first two weekends of the season – a perilously small sample size – City are the team most likely to dethrone Mikel Arteta's men. As they took Crystal Palace apart last Friday, they were a contradiction of familiarity and change. Maresca was on the backroom staff when Guardiola's side won the treble in 2022/23, but only Ruben Dias, Phil Foden and Erling Haaland remain from that team. The sight of Haaland smirking as he plunders goals in late summer is one of comforting familiarity, but don't let that persuade you City are the same. They're not.
Bernardo Silva, John Stones, Rodri, Nathan Ake and Jack Grealish all started the 2023 Champions League final against Inter Milan at the Ataturk Stadium. They all left during this window, a year on from fellow Istanbul starters Ilkay Gundogan, Kevin De Bruyne, Ederson and Manuel Akanji departing.
This goes a long way to explaining City's vast outlay over the past 18 months. Since January 2025, they have spent over $1billion on new players. Considerable funds have also come in — $431.6m this summer alone. Opposition fans and pundits have expressed plenty of frustration that all of this activity has gone on while the wait for a verdict in the Premier League's so-called 115 charges case against City goes on interminably.
As Guardiola's penultimate season collapsed in the face of an injury and confidence crisis that was captured in such gripping fashion in the recently released Amazon documentary "A Beautiful Obsession", City sprang into action. Their summer windows in 2024 and 2025 did not hit the mark. City have won one Champions League knockout tie since the 2023 final.
Outgoing sporting director Txiki Begiristain and his successor Hugo Viana worked at a furious pace, but there were more misses than hits. Of the 2025 signings, Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, Tijjani Reijnders and James Trafford were all moved on during this window, albeit for handsome fees. Only the Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov of the players signed last year can be considered unqualified successes.
Marc Guehi and Antoine Semenyo were smart pieces of January 2026 business who helped take the title race against Arsenal to the final week. Semenyo also netted a brilliant winning goal against Chelsea in the FA Cup final
After plenty of their 2025 punts didn't come off, Viana and City have predominantly shopped for top-end talent this summer. Elliot Anderson became their record signing when he joined for £116m from Nottingham Forest, while Ayyoub Bouaddi arrived as one of the most highly regarded teenagers in Europe. Iliman Ndiaye was a late, opportunistic move, but the skilful Senegal attacker will be a better fit than Marmoush and is a notable upgrade.
These signings in support of Haaland and fast-developing talents such as Cherki, Jeremy Doku, Josko Gvardiol and Nico O'Reilly mean Maresca has an enviable squad at his disposal, along with impressive depth at centre-back.
It's a lot of change, and there will be teething problems. These aren't just transfer fees; these are human beings with new jobs and a new boss, moving families to a new city or country. Rough and smooth are inevitable.
But City's final signing of the window, which equals the British transfer record, is one that truly changes the feel.
Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855
— Manchester City (@ManCity) September 1, 2026
Enzo Fernandez was Maresca's man, but getting him through the door went right up to the deadline because it was never likely to be easy.
Relations between City and Chelsea had become strained after the Italian left Stamford Bridge in the middle of last season and bided his time to take over from Guardiola. Then consider Fernandez's wider reputation due to his antics as Argentina'sWorld Cup provocateur. More seriously, there was the incident when he streamed himself singing a racially offensive song on the national team bus after the 2024 Copa America final.
But Maresca worked with Fernandez in the 18 months after that flashpoint and had no doubt he was the key piece to temper City's loss of hard-bitten winners. It would have been easier not to get involved, to allow the excuse of change being gradual and hard, but Viana and the board backed their manager.
Maresca has the player he wanted, who completes a $435.7m midfield refit. He knows Fernandez changes expectations, and he chose to demand those high stakes. Enzo and Anderson must lay the platform for Cherki, Semenyo, Ndiaye, Phil Foden, and Haaland to shine.
That's a group of players that must challenge strongly for the grandest prizes. No top-four as something to build on. An Arsenal procession or an early Champions League exit cannot be explained away with talk of transition. Nor would Maresca's bosses attempt to do so.
"This machine is built to win," said City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak on the aforementioned Amazon doc. "It doesn't work if we don't win."

23h03
Ce live est désormais terminé
Merci d’avoir suivi avec nous les dernières infos de ce conflit, marqué ce mardi par une nouvelle flambée de violences.
23h00
Wall Street recule, crispée par la situation géopolitique
La Bourse de New York a terminé en baisse mardi sous le poids des inquiétudes économiques liées à la reprise des hostilités entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran, qui fait grimper pétrole et taux d’intérêt.
Le Dow Jones a cédé 0,79 %, l’indice Nasdaq a perdu 1,03 % et l’indice élargi a lâché 0,71 %.
22h33
Le Croissant-Rouge fait état de 4 morts lors d’un mariage après une frappe américaine
Le Croissant-Rouge iranien a annoncé mardi que quatre personnes, dont un enfant, avaient été tuées et plus de 50 autres blessées lors d’une attaque américaine alors qu’elles assistaient à un mariage dans le sud du pays. Un peu plus tôt, un dirigeant iranien avait évoqué deux morts lors de ce mariage.
21h21
La télévision iranienne fait état de blessés lors d’un mariage après une frappe américaine
La télévision d’Etat iranienne rapporte qu’une frappe américaine sur le sud du pays a fait « plusieurs blessés parmi des habitants qui assistaient à une cérémonie de mariage ». Selon la chaîne, la frappe a touché un « quartier résidentiel » dans la province de Sirik. Selon un responsable iranien, deux personnes seraient mortes.
21h10
Le prix du gaz européen au plus haut depuis 2023 après les frappes en Iran
Le prix du gaz européen bondit de plus de 6 % mardi et touche un niveau plus vu depuis plus de trois ans en raison de la reprise des hostilités entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran. Vers 19 heures GMT, le contrat à terme du TTF néerlandais, considéré comme la référence européenne, prenait 6,20 % à 74,14 euros le mégawattheure, au plus haut depuis janvier 2023.
20h45
L’Iran lance une « opération décisive » contre des cibles américaines
L’Iran a débuté sa riposte en ciblant des intérêts américains au Moyen-Orient après une nouvelle salve d’attaques des Etats-Unis, rapporte l’agence de presse iranienne Tasnim. « Une opération décisive menée par les forces armées iraniennes en riposte à l’ennemi américain a commencé », a écrit Tasnim. « Les bases et les intérêts américains dans la région sont pris pour cible par des missiles et des drones iraniens ».
20h23
Un aéroport du sud de l’Iran visé par une frappe américaine
Un aéroport du sud de l’Iran, dans la province de Kerman, a été visé par une frappe américaine, a rapporté la télévision d’Etat iranienne. « Il y a quelques minutes, une attaque de l’ennemi américain a ciblé l’aéroport de Jiroft », a indiqué la télévision d’Etat, sans faire état dans l’immédiat de victimes ou de dégâts, après d’autres tirs sur le sud du pays près du détroit d’Ormuz.
20h12
De nouvelles explosions entendues près du détroit d’Ormuz
De nouvelles explosions ont été entendues mardi dans le sud de l’Iran, a rapporté la télévision d’Etat, qui avait déjà fait état d’autres déflagrations peu de temps auparavant. « Des explosions ont de nouveau été entendues dans la ville de Bandar Abbas et sur l’île de Qeshm », mais aussi sur l’île de Lavan située dans le Golfe et qui abrite l’un des terminaux d’exportation de pétrole iranien, a déclaré la télévision d’Etat.
20h08
Le baril de pétrole américain bondit de 5 % après les nouvelles frappes en Iran
Les cours du pétrole ont bondi après les nouvelles frappes menées par Washington en Iran et les menaces de Donald Trump, le baril WTI américain repassant le seuil des 90 dollars pour la première fois depuis fin juillet. Vers 17h55 GMT, le prix du baril de WTI gagnait 5,03 % à 90,07 dollars tandis que celui de son équivalent européen, le baril de Brent, prenait 4,5 % à 94,56 dollars.
19h58
L’Iran fera « regretter » aux Etats-Unis leurs nouvelles attaques
Les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens assurent qu’ils feraient « regretter » aux Etats-Unis leurs nouvelles attaques près du détroit d’Ormuz. « Un châtiment sévère attend les agresseurs. Les Etats-Unis regretteront leurs nouvelles attaques », a déclaré leur porte-parole, Hussein Mohebi, dans un message publié sur X.
19h39
Trump promet de bombarder l’Iran « bien plus durement » si le pays réplique
Donald Trump a menacé de bombarder l’Iran « bien plus durement » si le pays répliquait aux frappes menées mardi par l’armée américaine, qu’il a qualifiées de « puissantes ».
« Si la nation en faillite qu’est l’Iran riposte à cette attaque parfaitement justifiée, elle sera de nouveau frappée, bien plus durement », a écrit le président américain sur son réseau Truth Social.
19h11
Quatre projectiles ont frappé des villes à l’est du détroit d’Ormuz
Quatre projectiles ont frappé des villes à l’est du détroit d’Ormuz, selon plusieurs médias d’Etat iraniens.
18h47
Plusieurs explosions entendues dans le sud de l’Iran, près du détroit d’Ormuz
Plusieurs explosions ont été entendues mardi dans le sud de l’Iran, près du stratégique détroit d’Ormuz, a rapporté la télévision d’Etat iranienne, peu après l’annonce par l’armée américaine de nouvelles frappes.
Les déflagrations ont retenti près de Bandar Abbas et de l’île de Qeshm, a indiqué la chaîne, précisant qu'« aucun dégât » n’avait été signalé jusqu’à présent dans la province.
18h36
L’armée américaine annonce avoir déclenché des frappes contre l’Iran
Le Commandement militaire américain pour le Moyen-Orient (Centcom) annonce avoir déclenché de nouvelles frappes contre l’Iran, dans une courte déclaration publiée sur le réseau X.
« Aujourd’hui à 12h00 (18 heures à Paris), les forces américaines ont commencé à frapper des cibles des Gardiens de la révolution en Iran », a indiqué le Centcom, disant répondre « à de récentes attaques des Gardiens de la révolution contre la navigation commerciale dans le détroit d’Ormuz et contre des militaires américains déployés dans la région. »
14h11
Le président iranien rencontre Poutine au Kirghizistan et le remercie pour son soutien
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian a remercié mardi son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine pour sa position dans la guerre au Moyen-Orient, en marge du sommet de l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai (OCS) au Kirghizstan.
« Nous (...) vous remercions pour vos prises de position à chaque étape, tant durant la période où les combats et les actes d'agression étaient en cours que dans les circonstances normales, lorsque les Etats-Unis nous imposaient des sanctions », a-t-il déclaré.
12h00
Le président iranien affirme que les pressions et menaces américaines font dérailler la diplomatie
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian estime ce mardi que la stratégie américaine de pressions et de menaces risquaient de nuire aux efforts diplomatiques visant à mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient.
« L'absence de garanties » permettant d'assurer le respect par les Etats-Unis du protocole d'accord de juin « ainsi qu'un retour à une politique de pressions et de menaces risquent de faire dérailler la voie diplomatique », a déclaré M. Pezeshkian lors d'un sommet de l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai au Kirghizstan.
10h15
Un navire touché par trois « projectiles » dans le détroit d'Ormuz
Un tanker a été touché par trois « projectiles inconnus » alors qu'il quittait le détroit d'Ormuz, a annoncé mardi l'agence maritime britannique, UKMTO. « Un tanker a signalé avoir été frappé par trois projectiles inconnus alors qu'il achevait un transit sortant du détroit d'Ormuz. Aucune victime ni impact environnemental n'ont été signalés », a écrit l'UKMTO sur X, précisant que l'incident s'était produit à 17 milles nautiques (31 km) à l'est de Khasab (Oman).
La société de sécurité maritime Vanguard Tech a ensuite identifié le navire comme le Senegal Prosperity, battant pavillon libérien.
Elle a précisé que des « roquettes ont touché le navire sur son flanc bâbord, la salle des machines et un ballast, provoquant une perte des communications ». L'équipage est sain et sauf, a-t-elle indiqué.
08h20
L'Iran promet que Téhéran renouera « immédiatement » avec ses engagements si Washington revient à l'accord de juin
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian affirme ce mardi que Téhéran renouerait « immédiatement » avec ses engagements si les Etats-Unis revenaient au protocole d'accord conclu en juin pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient.
« Je déclare explicitement que si les Etats-Unis reviennent à leurs engagements au titre du protocole d'accord (...), la République islamique d'Iran prendra immédiatement des mesures réciproques », a déclaré Massoud Pezeshkian lors d'un sommet de l'Organisation de coopération de Shanghai au Kirghizstan, selon le site de la présidence iranienne.
08h10
Trump menace de bombarder « fort » l'Iran après la reprise des frappes
«Il y aura une réponse » et « nous allons les frapper fort », a averti le président américain, selon des propos retranscrits par la chaîne Fox News. Donald Trump a aussi affirmé, selon Fox News, que l'ensemble des missiles iraniens tirés avaient été interceptés, sauf un qui ne représentait pas une menace.
08h01
Les cours du pétrole sont repartis à la hausse lundi
Alors que le conflit est entré dans son septième mois et que les négociations sont au point mort, ce regain des hostilités a semé l'inquiétude sur les marchés: les cours du pétrole sont repartis en hausse, le baril de Brent, référence internationale, dépassant le seuil symbolique des 90 dollars.

It’s a huge day in the world of soccer, with the window about to slam shut for transfer deals for teams competing in Europe’s biggest leagues.
 
As has so often been the case in recent years, teams in the English Premier League have been the biggest spenders, with the $167 million deal to take French World Cup star Bradley Barcola from PSG to Liverpool earlier this week the most expensive transfer of the summer window so far.
As of Tuesday morning, a massive 1,270 transfers have taken place during the summer window, with those deals totaling an eye-opening $7.6 billion in transfer fees. In terms of the deals that could still be done before Tuesday’s deadline, the biggest transfer could involve Julián Alvarez. The Atletico Madrid striker wants a move to Barcelona, with EPL champion Arsenal also keen to sign the Argentine.
 
Crystal Palace’s Senegal forward Ismaila Sarr is also a reported late target for EPL rivals Liverpool. Meanwhile, USMNT World Cup star Folarin Balogun could make a switch from Monaco to Premier League Everton, while big-spending Chelsea are linked with a last-gasp move for Monaco’s Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara.
What time do the transfer windows close in the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A and Ligue 1?
The five largest European leagues all close their transfer windows on Tuesday, Sept. 1. Here’s a breakdown of the cut-off point for deals in each of the key leagues.
 
• English Premier League: 11 p.m. BST local time (6 p.m. ET)
• La Liga: Midnight CEST local time (6 p.m. ET)
• Serie A: 8 p.m. CEST local time (2 p.m. ET)
• Bundesliga: 8 p.m. CEST local time (2 p.m. ET)
• French Ligue 1: 11 p.m. CEST local time (5 p.m. ET)
 
It’s worth noting that clubs in the Dutch Eredivisie and the MLS in the US can sign players until Wednesday, Sept. 2. The Scottish SPL window, meanwhile, closes at 5 p.m. BST on Thursday, Sept. 3, with Austria and Belgium also open until that day.

Ship tracking firms reported that two supertankers carrying crude oil from Saudi Arabia were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night.
The tankers were struck by “unknown projectiles” within minutes of each other while passing through the strait near midnight.
The two Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCC), the Saudi-flagged Sidr and Liberia-flagged Senegal Prosperity, each loaded cargoes of about two million barrels of crude oil from Saudi Arabia’s Juaymah terminal last week.
WATCH — President Trump: I’m the Last Person to Trust Iran:
Saudi Arabia’s national oil company, Aramco, suspended loading from the Persian Gulf terminal of Juaymah in February due to a structural collapse. The suspension was extended during the Iran conflict until Juayman was finally reactivated in mid-August. Another suspended Persian Gulf terminal at Ras Tanura was reactivated after a four-month suspension in June.
Aramco has been selling oil from Juayman and Ras Tanura via ship-to-ship transfers off the coast of Fujairah, a port in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on the coast of the Gulf of Oman.
According to the Athens-based Marisks ship tracking firm, the Sidr was hit by unknown projectiles while sailing about 16.6 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman.
A few minutes later, the Senegal Prosperity was hit by three projectiles while sailing about half a nautical mile further northeast of Khasab. The attack on Senegal Prosperity was confirmed by the United Kingdom Maritime Operations (UKMTO) center.
“No casualties or environmental impact has been reported. Authorities are investigating. Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activities to UKMTO,” the center said.
Maritime security firm Vanguard said the three projectiles launched at Senegal Prosperity were rockets, and they struck the ship on its port side, engine room, and ballast tank.
“The near-simultaneous incidents represent a further escalation in the threat environment within the Omani corridor,” Marisks said.
President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Strait of Hormuz is in “very good shape” and under U.S. control.
“Many, many ships got through last night, as you know, with the Navy’s assistance, and we’ve been averaging 30 ships a night,” Trump said.
“That’s a lot, and a lot of oil is coming out. That’s why you haven’t seen the price of oil go like they thought it might have to go,” he said.
Oil prices rose on both Monday and Tuesday as the markets reacted to renewed hostility in the Strait of Hormuz. The European benchmark, Brent crude, rose to $91.48 per barrel, while America’s benchmark West Texas Intermediate hit $86.97 per barrel.
“Despite satellite tracking firms suggesting oil flowing through Hormuz is around 6 million barrels per day, that is well below pre-conflict levels,” said analysts from ANZ in Australia and New Zealand.
“In the meantime, the buffers the global oil market has been relying on are becoming exhausted. U.S. inventories are nearing minimum levels, while China’s ability to keep imports low will be tested as seasonal demand picks up,” ANZ added.

L’absence d’accès aux sites nucléaires iraniens, un problème urgent, selon l’AIEA
L’absence d’accès aux sites nucléaires iraniens pour y vérifier le matériel nucléaire « doit être réglée avec la plus grande urgence », souligne l’agence internationale de l’énergie atomique (AIEA) dans un rapport confidentiel.
« L’absence d’informations de l’Agence concernant ce matériau nucléaire et d’accès aux installations permettant de le vérifier constitue un motif de préoccupation en matière de prolifération », ajoute le gardien de la sûreté nucléaire de l’ONU dans ce rapport.
L’UE va lancer une mission de formation de l’armée au Liban
L’Union européenne va lancer une mission de formation de l’armée libanaise dans les prochains mois, mais sans remplacer la mission actuelle des Nations unies, a indiqué mardi sa cheffe de la diplomatie Kaja Kallas.
« Les ministres ont discuté de nos projets pour une nouvelle mission de l’UE visant à conseiller et former les forces armées du pays, notamment en matière de sécurité des frontières et de sécurité maritime », a-t-elle déclaré à l’issue d’une réunion des ministres de la défense de l’UE à Wicklow, près de Dublin. Elle a précisé que l’objectif était de parvenir en octobre à une décision formelle de lancement de cette mission.
Plusieurs explosions entendues près du détroit d’Ormuz
Plusieurs explosions ont été entendues mardi dans le sud de l’Iran, près du stratégique détroit d’Ormuz, a rapporté la télévision d’État iranienne, peu après l’annonce par l’armée américaine de nouvelles frappes. Les déflagrations ont retenti près de Bandar Abbas et de l’île de Qeshm, a indiqué la chaîne, précisant qu’« aucun dégât » n’avait été signalé jusqu’à présent dans la province.

L’armée américaine annonce avoir déclenché des frappes contre l’Iran
Le Commandement militaire américain pour le Moyen-Orient (Centcom) a annoncé mardi avoir déclenché de nouvelles frappes contre l’Iran, dans une courte déclaration publiée sur le réseau X.

L’Iran appelle ses citoyens à réduire leur consommation d’essence
Un haut responsable iranien a appelé ses concitoyens à réduire leur consommation d’essence, alors que Téhéran est confronté à des difficultés d’importation du fait du blocus naval imposé par les États-Unis.
« En tout état de cause, ce qui est clair, c’est que nous devons économiser l’essence dans notre consommation », a déclaré lors d’une allocution télévisée Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, président du Parlement qui a mené les négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre. « Si nous la consommons correctement, nous pouvons nous débrouiller avec la quantité d’essence que nous produisons », a-t-il ajouté, l’Iran étant l’un des principaux producteurs mondiaux de pétrole.
Israël menace le Royaume-Uni de représailles en cas de sanctions britanniques
Le ministre israélien des affaires étrangères a prévenu mardi 1er septembre que son pays répliquerait à d’éventuelles sanctions britanniques contre Israël, au moment où Londres dit préparer des mesures en lien avec les attaques de colons en Cisjordanie occupée.
« Si le Royaume-Uni agit contre l’État d’Israël, alors l’État d’Israël agira contre le Royaume-Uni », a déclaré le ministre Gideon Saar au principal site d’information israélien, Ynet. « Nous en avons les moyens », a-t-il ajouté.
Le président iranien remercie Poutine
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian a remercié, en marge d’un sommet régional au Kirghizstan, son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine pour sa position dans la guerre au Moyen-Orient, première rencontre entre les deux dirigeants depuis le début du conflit.
« Nous (…) vous remercions pour vos prises de position à chaque étape, tant durant la période où les combats et les actes d’agression étaient en cours que dans les circonstances normales, lorsque les États-Unis nous imposaient des sanctions », a-t-il déclaré. « Cela montre que notre relation est une relation stratégique, pas une relation ordinaire », a ajouté Massoud Pezeshkian.
Le médiateur qatarien exhorte l’Iran et les États-Unis à reprendre les négociations
Le médiateur qatarien a appelé les États-Unis et l’Iran à revenir à la table des négociations après le premier échange de frappes entre les deux pays en un mois.
« Nous avons dit dès le premier jour que laisser la question en suspens et tenter de normaliser la fermeture du détroit (d’Ormuz) conduirait à une escalade », a déclaré le porte-parole du ministère qatarien des affaires étrangères, Majed al-Ansari, lors d’un point de presse à Doha.
« Nous appelons les parties à faire preuve de sagesse et à revenir à la table des négociations, et nous continuons à intensifier nos efforts avec nos partenaires » dans cette médiation, a-t-il ajouté, parlant du Pakistan et d’Oman.
Le président iranien rencontre Poutine au Kirghizstan
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian s’est entretenu avec son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine, a annoncé Téhéran, première rencontre entre les deux dirigeants depuis le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient.

« Les deux parties ont fait un point sur l’état actuel des relations bilatérales et discuté des moyens de renforcer et d’élargir leur coopération dans divers domaines », selon un communiqué de la présidence iranienne, accompagné de photos des deux hommes se serrant la main.
Des colons israéliens tentent d’incendier une mosquée
Des colons israéliens ont tenté de mettre le feu à une mosquée en Cisjordanie occupée, territoire où les attaques contre les Palestiniens se multiplient, a annoncé le ministère palestinien des affaires religieuses. Selon le ministère, « un groupe de colons a tenté d’incendier des parties de la mosquée Nour al-Din al-Zanki », dans le village de Bazariya, près de Naplouse, dans le nord du territoire palestinien, laissant des graffitis en hébreu sur les murs.

Trois personnes tuées lors d’une opération à Gaza
Trois personnes ont été tuées à Gaza lors d’une opération israélienne visant à arrêter un haut responsable du Hamas, durant laquelle des bombardements d’une intensité rare ces dernières semaines ont été menés, selon les autorités locales.

Selon l’Iran, la politique américaine de pressions fait dérailler la diplomatie
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian a estimé que la stratégie américaine de pressions et de menaces risquaient de nuire aux efforts diplomatiques visant à mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient.
« L’absence de garanties » permettant d’assurer le respect par les États-Unis du protocole d’accord de juin « ainsi qu’un retour à une politique de pressions et de menaces risquent de faire dérailler la voie diplomatique », a déclaré Massoud Pezeshkian lors d’un sommet de l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghaï au Kirghizstan.
Le PAM réduit son aide alimentaire en Cisjordanie
Le Programme alimentaire mondial des Nations unies (PAM) a annoncé mardi 1er septembre réduire de moitié son aide alimentaire en Cisjordanie en raison du manque de financements, ramenant à 200 000 le nombre de bénéficiaires.
« Le PAM est contraint de réduire de moitié le nombre de personnes que nous aidons en Cisjordanie. Et cela alors que les besoins alimentaires en Cisjordanie ont plus que doublé par rapport à il y a deux ans », a déclaré à Genève un représentant de l’organisation en territoire palestinien, Shaun Hughes. « Nous sommes à court de fonds, ce qui signifie qu’à partir d’aujourd’hui, quelque 200 000 personnes n’auront plus accès à une aide vitale », a-t-il ajouté.
PAM estime que 900 000 personnes sont en situation d’insécurité alimentaire en Cisjordanie. C’est plus d’un quart de la population, alors qu’il y a deux ans, ce chiffre était de 11 %. « La recrudescence des violences commises par les colons et les déplacements de population perturbent les moyens de subsistance, aggravent la faim et plongent les familles toujours plus profondément dans la crise », indique l’organisation dans un communiqué.
Téhéran prêt à revenir à l’accord de juin dernier avec Washington
Le président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian a affirmé que Téhéran renouerait « immédiatement » avec ses engagements si les États-Unis revenaient au protocole d’accord conclu en juin pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient.
« Je déclare explicitement que si les États-Unis reviennent à leurs engagements au titre du protocole d’accord (…), la République islamique d’Iran prendra immédiatement des mesures réciproques », a déclaré Massoud Pezeshkian lors d’un sommet de l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghaï au Kirghizstan, selon le site de la présidence iranienne.
Le protocole d’accord visait à mettre durablement fin à la guerre entre Téhéran et Washington, déclenchée fin février par des frappes américaines et israéliennes contre la République islamique. Il a ensuite volé en éclats en juillet, les deux camps s’accusant mutuellement d’en avoir violé les termes.
Deux pétroliers touchés par des projectiles inconnus à Ormuz
Deux pétroliers ont été touchés par « des projectiles d’origine inconnue » alors qu’ils sortaient du détroit d’Ormuz, a-t-on appris mardi auprès de l’agence maritime grecque Marisks.
Mardi matin, l’agence maritime britannique UKMTO avait indiqué sur X qu’un tanker avait été touché par trois « projectiles inconnus » alors qu’il quittait le détroit d’Ormuz. Selon UMKO « aucune victime ni impact environnemental n’ont été signalés ». La société de sécurité maritime Vanguard Tech a identifié le navire comme le Senegal Prosperity, battant pavillon libérien.
Marisks a ensuite indiqué qu’au total « deux pétroliers transportant du brut ont été frappés par des projectiles d’origine inconnue à quelques minutes d’intervalle alors qu’ils se dirigeaient vers la sortie du détroit d’Ormuz lundi soir ». Outre le Senegal property, le tanker Sidr battant pavillon saoudien a également été ciblé, selon Marisks.
La société grecque souligne que « ces incidents quasi simultanés représentent une nouvelle escalade du niveau de menace » dans le détroit d’Ormuz.

‘Since It Is a Black Cemetery and Has the Stigma of Slavery, No One Wants to Touch It’
Editor’s note: This story is part of a special series by Princeton University journalism students reporting on the discovery of an African burial ground in Key West, Florida, and how the legacy of slavery still reverberates through the island community and beyond.
I t’s a breezy Sunday morning in March at Higgs Beach in Key West. The Straits of Florida glisten and the sun leaves a feeling of hazy contentment. Bright pink flags and a yellow sign announce the Key West Orchid Society’s annual orchid show, hosted at the Key West Garden Club. A freckled purple flower, contestant No. 298, is vying for top honors.
Just across the sidewalk from the West Martello Tower, a Civil War-era fort where the Garden Club is housed, lies an unkempt field of grass, worn out by dehydration and footsteps. Beneath the plot sit six unmarked graves, and across the busy throughway of Atlantic Boulevard, over 100 more. Dogs run joyously next to the 100 graves — a fenced-in dog park, a locals’ enclave on an island otherwise thirsting for open space.

For more than 15 years, officials in Key West and surrounding Monroe County have known about those unmarked graves, which date to 1860 and hold the remains of some 295 Africans who’d been rescued with hundreds more from illegal slave ships and brought to shore, only to die a few weeks later of illnesses like yellow fever and dysentery. A decorative concrete memorial covers the first 15 graves found nearby in 2002, but nothing identifies the location of the bodies that remain.
The story of why these graves remain unmarked is one of local gripes and bureaucratic red tape, but it also raises questions of whose lives deserved to be honored and which histories should be remembered. As a liberal enclave in an otherwise conservative state, Key West is already under attack when it comes to how public spaces are utilized and public funds are spent: The Florida Department of Transportation removed rainbow crosswalks in the city last year, and a new state law limiting government funding for projects and events deemed to be pro-DEI (diversity, equity, and inclusion) threatens Key West’s festivals — including, potentially, future initiatives at the African burial ground.
“Since it is a Black cemetery and it has the stigma of slavery, nobody wants to touch it,” says Veronica Stafford, a longtime local activist, of the stagnant situation at Higgs Beach.
Some local politicians see the causes of inaction differently. “At some point, you don’t keep expending taxpayer money on something that’s not going to come to fruition,” Heather Carruthers, a Monroe County commissioner from 2008 to 2020, says. “[The county] tried for years to do something about it.”
Now, an ownership transfer of Higgs Beach Park from Monroe County to the City of Key West, initiated May 1, has reignited the question of development at Higgs Beach, and along with it, the graves underneath the surface.
ON A HOT, CLEAR DAY in September 2002, a small crowd gathered for a ceremony at Higgs Beach where the first 15 graves had been found. A wobbly fence surrounded the area, located on a patch of sand next to two palm trees and near the West Martello Tower. “African Cemetery 1860,” read a makeshift sign roped onto the fence. Adegbolu Adefunmi, a Yoruba leader, performed a ritual.
The year before, a state historic marker had been installed. “Near this site lie the remains of the 294 African men, women and children who died in Key West in 1860,” the sign reads — one off from the correct count of 295, which includes a six-week-old child who had died early on. But those were minor wins in the battle to more fully and respectfully recognize the burial ground.
In April 2005, a dog park — split into sections for small and large dogs — opened across the street from the fenced-off gravesite. But the grounds received little attention otherwise. By the time Carruthers was elected to the Monroe County Board of Commissioners in 2008, Higgs Beach had fallen into neglect. Carruthers, a former classical vocalist from New York who owned a well-known guesthouse on the island, was determined to address the problem.
“Higgs Beach was in disrepair. It was becoming a haven for the homeless and local people didn’t want to use it,” Carruthers, now a business development director at the architecture firm K2M Design, said in an interview at the company’s Key West office in March. “A lot of people felt like it wasn’t safe.” Her goal was to “reinvigorate the park,” and local architect William Horn was tapped to lead the development process and get feedback from community members.
In 2010, after preliminary meetings had been held with key stakeholders, marine archaeologist Corey Malcom, who had spearheaded the discovery of the first 15 graves, and Dinizulu Gene Tinnie, an artist who led the design of the African Cemetery Memorial that now covers them, raised the possibility of additional unmarked graves in the area. “I said, ‘OK, you guys are making all these wonderful plans, but you need to know, there’s a lot of people in that park somewhere, and they’re missing, and we haven’t found them,’” Malcom says.
So, a new ground-penetrating-radar survey of the area was commissioned by the county. The results — displayed in rows of blurry squiggles on the radar diagrams — showed more than 100 distinct graves beneath the small-dog park, with more likely located underneath the road, where GPR could not reach. That December, in response to the discovery, a plan was presented to move the small-dog park and shift Atlantic Boulevard, a main thoroughfare along the coast, north so the entire gravesite could be unified into a green space.
“The location of these graves is a significant archaeological discovery, one of the only known cemeteries of African refugees in the United States, and presents an opportunity for preservation of this historic discovery,” the development master plan read.
However, not everyone was happy about the proposed changes. Community members concerned about the new road’s proximity to their houses requested additional meetings with Carruthers and Horn. The group, calling themselves the Higgs Beach Preservation Committee, had a range of other objections as well. (Among them, a chain link fence for the dog park did not meet a high enough “aesthetic character.”) A compromise was struck, and after adjusted plans were approved by the Key West Planning Board, a development agreement was formed between the county and city in 2012.
But there would be a new roadblock. A community member who opposed the redevelopment plan found a 1983 grant from the U.S. Department of the Interior, through the Land and Water Conservation Fund, which stipulated the scope of development permitted within the park, and that major changes had to be approved by the federal government. Atlantic Boulevard could not be moved without approval from the Department of the Interior.
Faced with the lengthy process of obtaining federal approval, county officials left the park largely untouched for years. The small-dog park remained on top of the 100 African graves — though pets are prohibited from frolicking in the island’s other cemeteries. With redevelopment plans in limbo, county officials also didn’t move to commemorate the unmarked graves in any physical way. The county did, however, in May 2012, apply successfully for the site to be named a National Historic Landmark.
IN 2017, NAJA AND ARNAUD Girard, the owners of The Blue Paper, an independent local publication that’s now defunct, learned about the unmarked graves after attending a Day of Remembrance ceremony for the slave trade and its abolition that is held annually at the African Cemetery Memorial. Before then, Arnaud says, he had “no idea” about the existence of the burial site. Moved by what they had learned, the couple decided to make a short documentary about the graves beneath the dog park, alongside journalist Amber Nolan.
The French-born Arnaud had come to America after law school, military service, and international travel that included sailing a boat alone across the Atlantic Ocean from Senegal to New York. In the United States, he met Naja, and the two moved to Key West in the mid-1980s. They became journalists for The Blue Paper while living with their kids on a boat off of Wisteria Island, and took over ownership of the paper in 2011. Right away, the Girards shifted some of its focus: They were interested in telling the story of Bahama Village, the historically Black community in Key West.
“One of the things that we had noticed,” Arnaud says, “is that the Black community was never talked about.”
That mission continued with their documentary about the burial site, Do All Graves Matter? With the help of Stafford, who features prominently in the film, they interviewed local leaders on camera. Clayton Lopez, then a Key West City Commissioner, stated that he wanted the dog park to be moved. Carruthers, who was not in town during filming, shared an email with the filmmakers outlining why progress was not being made on Higgs Beach redevelopment or the dog park, including challenges with funding and the approvals process.
According to the Girards, when they were getting ready to post the documentary to The Blue Paper’s website, local politicians including Carruthers tried to intervene. “All of a sudden, the phone starts ringing from every side,” Arnaud says.
Naja believes Carruthers “didn’t like the story because it was kind of embarrassing. Why are you saying this is a cemetery and then also saying this is a place for your dogs to poop?”
“If there’s anything that we did [to intervene] or to ask them to postpone any press, it was probably because at the time we were trying to negotiate with the federal government about changes to the the site that would allow us to better honor the graves that we knew were there,” Carruthers says in a follow-up phone call. “Our intention was always to try to change that park…and, in fact, move the road so that the souls that were buried there would have the appropriate kind of respect.”
The Girards went ahead with the release of their film in August 2017. Within a week, Monroe County confirmed plans to move the small-dog park into a portion of the large-dog park, leaving the land over the gravesite open. Still, the county’s announcement cast uncertainty on the presence of the graves, saying the move was made “out of an abundance of caution that there may be possible graves beneath the current small dog park.”
“I DON’T THINK IT’S EVER been proven that they are graves,” current Monroe County administrator Christine Hurley says at her office in the former E. H. Gato Cigar Factory, just a five-minute drive inland from Higgs Beach. She adds, citing the delicate nature of the undertaking, “I don’t think we want to excavate it to figure out if it’s really graves or not. … Anomalies are not for sure remains.”
As for the idea of marking the gravesite with any plaque or signage, Carruthers said in March that the county commissioners had never discussed the matter. “They felt, I think, that the African Memorial that’s there covers the whole space.”
Hurley echoes that sentiment, saying, “We believe there’s already a commemorative spot.”
Hurley also claims there is no current plan to move Atlantic Boulevard, despite the initial intention to unify the entirety of the gravesite. “The only reason the road was going to be moved was to get funding to improve the park,” she says. When the area’s Tourism Development Council changed an earlier position and said it could fund improvements on both sides of the road, rather than only the beach side, she explains, “the county dropped that request to try to move that road.”
Regardless, Monroe County didn’t want to own the park anymore, citing disagreements with the City of Key West over what should be built there and the distance of the park from the county’s other operations. At a March 5 City Commission meeting, an ownership transfer of the park from the county to the city was proposed. No mention of the gravesite was made at the meeting. On April 1, the Key West City Commission voted to approve the transfer, and the city officially took control on May 1.
Sam Kaufman, a former city commissioner and the recently inaugurated mayor of Key West, voted against the ownership transfer, citing the increased tax burden on Key West residents in case the park did not turn a profit one year. However, he said in a March interview that, if elected, he would take steps to commemorate the graves.
“Would I do anything? One hundred percent. …First and foremost, better signage, not just for the graves, but also for the history,” Kaufman said, adding, “I would probably put a lot of weight on what people like Dr. Malcom say, people in the Art and Historical Society, people in the African American community.”
MEMBERS OF THE AFRICAN American community have aspirations not just for Higgs Beach, but for their presence in the city at large.
Arida Wright, an organizer of the Day of Remembrance ceremony at the African Cemetery Memorial, which is paid for largely through fundraising, says, “It would be nice just to have a grant” for the annual event. She dreams of having enough funds to cover “the performers we want to bring, the speakers we want to bring, not every year needing money and never having [it], having to raise the money.”
Tinnie, the artist who helped raise the alarm about possible additional graves, still believes the relocation of Atlantic Boulevard is a possibility, and suggests an “obelisk or something in the middle” of a roundabout near the African Cemetery Memorial and the neighboring AIDS memorial: “Something that lets people know you’ve entered a sacred space here.”
With the ownership transfer and a potentially sympathetic mayor, the future of the graves at Higgs Beach enters another period of hope and uncertainty. The city could take steps to acknowledge the location of the 100 unmarked graves, but the long-term future of the site is in question. The new state law that broadly prohibits local government funding for anything related to “DEI” may make renovations or an expanded memorial difficult.
In the meantime, local Black activists continue fighting for their history to be recognized and told.
Stafford, for one, wants a docent on hand. “That burial site should have someone there guiding the tourists that come along and come to check the site out with historical information,” she says. And when it comes to signage, she adds, “I would like to see a huge sign or billboard erected at the Higgs Beach where the cemetery is — the biggest billboard.”

Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Monday that the Islamic Republic will not hesitate to "respond decisively" to attacks, after the U.S. said it had carried out strikes on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
"The Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will have no hesitation in exercising their inherent right to self-defense and will respond decisively, as appropriate, to any military aggression by the enemy," the ministry said in a statement.

The most recent incident involving a commercial ship in the region reported by the U.K. Navy's Maritime Operations center, which monitors such attacks, was a tanker "struck by an unknown projectile whilst transiting inbound in the Strait of Hormuz" on Saturday.

U.S. military strikes 2 Iranian launchers on Larak Island, official says
U.S. forces on Sunday struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. Central Command spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins.
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets and deploy sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz, Hawkins said. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said Friday that U.S. forces had cleared all sea mines from the shipping lanes of the strait.
Larak Island sits in the Strait of Hormuz, just a few miles off Iran's coast, and Tehran is believed to have used the island as a de facto toll booth as it demands ships pay fees to transit the strategic waterway safely.
The IRGC, in a statement conveyed by Iran's state broadcaster, said "several of our fighters and compatriots" were killed and wounded in the U.S. strike, according to The Associated Press.
The statement said the attack would "result in punishment of the aggressor."
